guides.title: Why hold a stock for years instead of a day trade
guides.concept: Long-term holding rests on the company's business, valuation and multi-year risk assumptions; an intraday hold rests on a much shorter price-pattern thesis.
guides.watchFor: Read issuer filings, cash flow, products, margins, debt, dilution and valuation; define original assumptions and a calendar-based review process.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative long-term purchase needs primary-source company research, plausible valuation and acceptable concentration, rather than a one-minute candle.
guides.holdEvidence: A hypothetical hold remains coherent only while reported business performance and risk conditions broadly support the original thesis and investment horizon.
guides.exitEvidence: Review exit or reduction if the business deteriorates, debt or dilution violates assumptions, valuation no longer supports the case, or a personal liquidity goal changes.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for primary filings; NO TRADE when valuation, ownership objective or downside capacity cannot be articulated.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: An invented company's cash generation weakens while quarterly sales rise. Its one-day price bounce does not by itself restore the original multi-year investment thesis.
guides.procedure: Read issuer filings, cash flow, products, margins, debt, dilution and valuation; define original assumptions and a calendar-based review process.
guides.limit: This original educational framework is not a verified profitable strategy, personalized trading advice, an executable market quote or a prediction of future returns.
guides.invalidation: The original thesis fails, a key risk or exposure boundary is violated, or source data are unavailable; no planned exit level guarantees a market fill.
guides.commonError: Switching horizons after losses, confusing an observed indicator with a proven edge or using future data to rewrite a holding thesis.

guides.title: Long-term portfolio hold trim rebalance and diversification
guides.concept: Portfolio holding considers goals, asset mix, sector overlap and concentration independently of the attractiveness of any individual company.
guides.watchFor: Check target asset weights, current weights, fund holdings, time horizon, cash needs, trading costs and a previously recorded rebalance threshold.
guides.entryEvidence: A possible addition must fit the overall plan, not just a standalone bullish case; multiple funds can own the same concentrated underlying holdings.
guides.holdEvidence: A model hold is justified when exposure, liquidity and asset mix remain inside established policy boundaries, even after daily fluctuations.
guides.exitEvidence: Rebalance or trim under a predetermined schedule or drift rule, when goals change, or if a large single-position weight violates diversification policy.
guides.noTrade: WAIT when current allocations are unknown; NO TRADE when an allocation recommendation needs private financial circumstances not provided.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: One model holding climbs from 8% to 17% of a portfolio with a 10% position cap. Its good business outlook does not erase the portfolio's concentration limit.
guides.procedure: Check target asset weights, current weights, fund holdings, time horizon, cash needs, trading costs and a previously recorded rebalance threshold.

guides.title: Earnings reports guidance margins and cash-flow changes
guides.concept: Earnings-per-share surprises do not independently establish earnings quality or whether the company's future cash generation improved.
guides.watchFor: Verify issuer, report and acceptance times, revenues, margins, cash from operations, segments, management guidance and prior expectations.
guides.entryEvidence: A long-horizon hypothesis uses reported fundamentals and valuation; a day-trading catalyst setup separately needs the observed post-news price trigger and execution risk.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold reasoning depends on whether reported facts support the original business assumptions, not whether the first post-earnings candle is green.
guides.exitEvidence: Review exit if guidance cuts, debt risks, recurring-margin decline or weak cash conversion meaningfully challenge the thesis.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for the original 10-Q or 8-K and release chronology; NO TRADE if relevant numbers cannot be reconciled.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: Earnings beat estimates but operating cash flow falls and guidance is lowered. A headline beat alone cannot establish a better long-term holding thesis.
guides.procedure: Verify issuer, report and acceptance times, revenues, margins, cash from operations, segments, management guidance and prior expectations.

guides.title: Debt dilution cash flow and valuation based exit decisions
guides.concept: A share-price chart or low P/E is insufficient to assess business solvency, investment value, changing share count and financing risk.
guides.watchFor: Read audited balance-sheet, income and cash-flow statements; compare debt maturities, capital needs, issued shares and valuation assumptions.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative entry requires understanding cash and liabilities and a defensible range of possible outcomes, not a single stock-price multiple.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold reasoning may persist when leverage, cash generation and business prospects stay within the stated thesis.
guides.exitEvidence: Reevaluate after a financing crisis, dilution, accounting change, cash shortfall or sharply altered fair-value assumptions.
guides.noTrade: WAIT if filings are missing; NO TRADE when the conclusion depends on stale capital structure or unverified projections.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A company doubles its share count and reports unchanged net income. Total company profit is stable, but earnings per share decline under the larger denominator.

guides.title: Market trend breadth volatility and regime filter
guides.concept: Trend, volatility, breadth and participation describe a market environment; no single market-regime label predicts future returns.
guides.watchFor: Specify index, timeframe, advance/decline breadth, participation above averages, sector dispersion and volatility measured as of the pause.
guides.entryEvidence: An example setup requires its own trigger and risk plan; favorable index context may support but cannot replace stock-specific evidence.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold conditions include the original trade structure and any predeclared market-context condition staying intact.
guides.exitEvidence: Reassess if broad-market structure and volatility violate the setup's intended regime, or if the planned risk boundary fails.
guides.noTrade: WAIT if breadth is ambiguous; NO TRADE when a strategy designed for orderly trends encounters wide-spread chop.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: An index touches a new high while only 28% of its members advance and spreads widen. The headline high alone is not broad confirmation.
guides.procedure: Specify index, timeframe, advance/decline breadth, participation above averages, sector dispersion and volatility measured as of the pause.

guides.title: Sector rotation relative strength and concentrated exposures
guides.concept: Relative strength compares performance to a stated benchmark, not simply a stock or sector going up; sector leadership can rotate.
guides.watchFor: Choose benchmark, total-return convention, timeframe, ETF composition and sector classification before claiming leadership.
guides.entryEvidence: A hypothetical sector entry requires a verifiable comparison plus a stock-specific setup and controlled concentration.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold depends on the original sector exposure, company evidence and the declared relative-strength timeframe remaining coherent.
guides.exitEvidence: Review if measured leadership fails, sector fundamentals change or concentration rises above limits.
guides.noTrade: WAIT when benchmarks differ; NO TRADE if sector exposure would duplicate an already excessive portfolio position.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: Sector A rises 8% while the benchmark rises 12% over the same month. Sector A gained but underperformed; absolute gain is not relative leadership.
guides.procedure: Choose benchmark, total-return convention, timeframe, ETF composition and sector classification before claiming leadership.

guides.title: Conflicting daily five-minute and one-minute signals
guides.concept: Two charts can disagree because they refer to different periods; do not use an unfinished higher-timeframe candle or switch horizons after a loss.
guides.watchFor: State controlling thesis, context timeframe, trigger timeframe, completed-bar status and mandatory versus optional checklist conditions.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative entry must satisfy the governing setup's trigger, not just a convenient one-minute signal against major daily resistance.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold the original intraday premise only while its recorded structure and invalidation still apply; converting a scalp into a long-term hold is not disciplined analysis.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows governing-timeframe invalidation, liquidity loss or a risk breach rather than a retrospective change of timeframe.
guides.noTrade: WAIT while confirmation remains provisional; NO TRADE if mandatory chart conditions contradict one another.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A green one-minute bar appears under daily resistance while a five-minute breakout candle is unfinished. The five-minute close is not yet evidence.
guides.procedure: State controlling thesis, context timeframe, trigger timeframe, completed-bar status and mandatory versus optional checklist conditions.

guides.title: VWAP EMA volume disagreement and hard no-trade vetoes
guides.concept: Several indicators may reuse the same price information and are not statistically independent votes; a hard risk veto cannot be outweighed by three bullish colors.
guides.watchFor: Separate primary trigger, secondary context, source coverage, unfinished candles, live spread and liquidity constraints.
guides.entryEvidence: An example entry is only eligible when all mandatory checks pass; positive technical confluence cannot waive a nonnegotiable execution risk.
guides.holdEvidence: A hypothetical hold needs intact price structure and verified exposure, not a majority vote from indicators.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows objective invalidation or cost/exposure breach; do not revise the rule after viewing the outcome.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for missing confirmation; NO TRADE when spread, halt, borrow or stale-quote vetoes invalidate an otherwise attractive signal.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: EMA9, VWAP and momentum appear favorable, but a $0.45 spread on a $7 security violates a predeclared cost ceiling. Indicator agreement does not cancel the veto.
guides.procedure: Separate primary trigger, secondary context, source coverage, unfinished candles, live spread and liquidity constraints.

guides.title: Time and sales versus quotes and aggressive-trade inference
guides.horizon: Seconds to minutes: market data context
guides.concept: Executed prints and displayed bids/offers are different data; quote-relative tape colors depend on synchronization and vendor convention.
guides.watchFor: Check timestamps, reported trades, venue coverage, corrections, NBBO, spread and the platform's color assumptions.
guides.entryEvidence: An educational tape-based entry still needs a price-structure trigger and risk plan; a green print cannot identify an institution's motives.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold is conditional on the original price structure and risk, not an unverified cluster of ask-side colored prints.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows broken price response, widening spreads or inadequate liquidity, not a single print color change.
guides.noTrade: WAIT if quotes and prints cannot be synchronized; NO TRADE with incomplete or materially delayed feed information.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A 100-share execution is colored green by a chart because it matched an ask. That does not establish which institution traded or guarantee upward price movement.
guides.procedure: Check timestamps, reported trades, venue coverage, corrections, NBBO, spread and the platform's color assumptions.

guides.title: Level II depth hidden liquidity and partial fills
guides.concept: Displayed market depth is not complete liquidity. Quote size may cancel and a large order can fill at several prices or not at all.
guides.watchFor: Check feed venues, quote timestamp, visible size, price levels, prints, broker acknowledgments and remaining quantity.
guides.entryEvidence: An example entry requires feasible spread and size assumptions rather than reliance on a single large displayed bid.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold requires knowing the actual filled position and risk; a quote wall is not the same as completed buying.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows adverse depth changes, pending-cancel exposure, partial fills or violated risk assumptions.
guides.noTrade: WAIT for actual broker status; NO TRADE if visible depth is stale or order execution uncertainty prevents proper sizing.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: Only 300 shares are displayed at the best ask, but the learner models buying 1,000. A complete fill at the displayed top price cannot be assumed.
guides.procedure: Check feed venues, quote timestamp, visible size, price levels, prints, broker acknowledgments and remaining quantity.

guides.title: Long calls puts theta implied volatility and hold decisions
guides.concept: An option's value responds to stock direction, implied volatility, time decay, strike, dividends and contract terms; correct direction does not ensure profit.
guides.watchFor: Review premium paid, contract multiplier, strike, expiry, liquidity, delta, gamma, theta, vega and the stock thesis.
guides.entryEvidence: An example long option requires an expected move and horizon sufficient to justify premium risk, not simply a bullish chart.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold only if the price/timing thesis and acceptable premium-loss plan remain intact; changing volatility and time decay affect that reasoning.
guides.exitEvidence: Review exit when the premium risk limit, time stop, volatility change or expiry-exercise consequences undermine the case.
guides.noTrade: NO TRADE if total premium loss is not understood, or expiry, exercise, Greek or liquidity information is missing.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A call is bought for $2 per share. The underlying rises modestly while implied volatility collapses and time passes; the call can lose value despite the correct direction.
guides.procedure: Review premium paid, contract multiplier, strike, expiry, liquidity, delta, gamma, theta, vega and the stock thesis.

guides.title: Short option assignment dividend and expiration risk
guides.horizon: Options: through early exercise and expiration
guides.concept: Short American-style equity options can be assigned before expiration; premium collected is not a risk-free income stream.
guides.watchFor: Verify strike, premium, contract multiplier, expiry, exercise style, dividend date, assignment procedure, collateral and resulting stock obligations.
guides.entryEvidence: An illustrative short-premium case is analyzable only when the assignment and underlying exposure are understood and broker approval is verified.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold requires tolerable potential assignment and maintained collateral and risk limits, not an assumption that assignment is unlikely.
guides.exitEvidence: Review closure or protection around material exercise incentives, changed risk, dividend dates and expiration.
guides.noTrade: NO TRADE if assignment could create unaffordable delivery or purchase obligations, or broker rules are unknown.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A short call is deep in the money just before a dividend event. A trader may be assigned early even though the option has not expired.
guides.procedure: Verify strike, premium, contract multiplier, expiry, exercise style, dividend date, assignment procedure, collateral and resulting stock obligations.

guides.title: Vertical options spreads net Greeks and leg assignment
guides.concept: Spreads have multiple legs and net sensitivities; a limited theoretical expiration loss does not eliminate interim assignment, liquidity or execution risks.
guides.watchFor: Check each leg, expiry, strike, multiplier, net credit/debit, combined Greeks, liquidity and broker expiration handling.
guides.entryEvidence: Before entry analysis, establish a complete payoff model and operational understanding of partial fills and assignment exposure.
guides.holdEvidence: Hold only while all legs, risk assumptions, collateral and time limits remain compatible with the original plan.
guides.exitEvidence: Exit review follows leg assignment, unexpected stock exposure, risk limit, expiry deadline or breakdown of the underlying case.
guides.noTrade: NO TRADE when combined-leg settlement and exercise obligations cannot be modeled accurately.
guides.fictionalCase: FICTIONAL: A vertical spread displays a theoretical gain but its short leg is near early assignment. Paper gain does not eliminate possible interim stock exposure.
guides.procedure: Check each leg, expiry, strike, multiplier, net credit/debit, combined Greeks, liquidity and broker expiration handling.
